stem: A 49 year old presents to ED complaining of muscle weakness and clumsiness in the right hand, with slow and effortful speech. In which of the following lobes is the lesion most likely found:
fact: Right-hand weakness with expressive dysphasia localizes to the dominant left frontal lobe.
mnemonic: Left frontal: language plus opposite face/hand weakness.
finding: NCBI aphasia anatomy and contralateral motor localization support the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the parietal lobe:
fact: Hemispatial neglect is strongly associated with parietal-lobe dysfunction, particularly in the non-dominant hemisphere.
finding: Standard cortical functional anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: What type of visual field defect are you most likely to see in a lesion at the optic chiasm:
fact: Optic-chiasm lesions classically cause bitemporal hemianopia by affecting crossing nasal retinal fibres.
mnemonic: Chiasm cuts the crossing fields: both temporal fields go.

stem: A 68 year old lady was involved in a road traffic accident and describes a whiplash type injury. She has pain and tenderness in the cervical region and imaging shows a herniated disc in this region. The patient is complaining of weakness of elbow extension and loss of sensation over the middle finger. Which of the following spinal nerves is most likely affected:
fact: C7 contributes to elbow extension through the triceps and sensory supply around the middle finger.
mnemonic: C7: triceps and the middle finger.
finding: C7 myotome and dermatome localization supports the displayed key; no figure is required for the source question.

stem: CSF is reabsorbed from subarachnoid space via which of the following structures:
fact: Arachnoid granulations transfer CSF from the subarachnoid space into dural venous sinuses.
mnemonic: Granulations drain CSF to venous sinuses.
finding: Standard CSF physiology supports the displayed key.

stem: Cerebrospinal fluid is primarily produced by which of the following structures:
fact: CSF is primarily produced by the choroid plexus, with most production arising from the lateral ventricular plexuses.
finding: Standard CSF physiology supports the displayed key.

stem: The Broca's speech area is located in which of the following regions:
fact: Broca area lies in the inferior frontal region of the dominant hemisphere and supports speech production.
mnemonic: Broca builds speech in the frontal lobe.
finding: NCBI supports the displayed key; source apostrophe wording is retained literally.

stem: Which of the following clinical features is most suggestive of a lesion of the temporal lobe:
options: Conjugate eye deviation towards the side of the lesion
fact: Receptive dysphasia is associated with dysfunction of the posterior temporal language area, traditionally termed Wernicke area.
mnemonic: Wernicke receives meaning in the temporal lobe.

stem: Which of the following clinical features would you least expect to see in a lesion of the frontal lobe:
options: Spastic paralysis of the contralateral leg
Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
fact: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing is classically an occipital visual-cortex sign, not a typical frontal-lobe sign.
mnemonic: Occipital sees fields; frontal plans and moves.
finding: NCBI occipital-lobe anatomy supports the displayed key.

stem: Which of the following is most likely to cause a bitemporal hemianopia:
fact: A pituitary adenoma can compress the optic chiasm and cause bitemporal hemianopia.
finding: NCBI supports the displayed key and source explanation.
